questions.question: Find the length of the longest pole that can be placed in a room of dimensions 30 m × 15 m × 10 m.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **longest pole** in a **rectangular room** is always the **diagonal** of the **cuboid**.

Diagonal = √(Length² + Breadth² + Height²)

Diagonal = √(30² + 15² + 10²) = √(900 + 225 + 100) = √1225 = 35 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length (L) = **30 m**

Breadth (B) = **15 m**

Height (H) = **10 m**

**Formula Used:**

Length of the **longest pole** = **Diagonal of the room** = √(L² + B² + H²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e9abf8a8849ac11d264efd675a3ffea7dda93b0008b8a5515f8bef08228d982.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Longest pole = √(30² + 15² + 10²)

⇒ Longest pole = √(900 + 225 + 100)

⇒ Longest pole = √1225

⇒ Longest pole = 35 m

**∴ The correct answer is 35 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total area covering all faces is given by 2(LB + BH + LH).

Volume of Cuboid

The space occupied by the cuboid is calculated as Length × Breadth × Height.

Lateral Surface Area

Area of the four walls of the room = 2 × Height × (Length + Breadth).</p

questions.question: A cuboid having the surface area of 3 adjacent faces as a, b, c has the volume:
questions.solution:
**Given: **

The Areas of 3 adjacent faces of cuboid = a, b & c 

**Formula used:**

The volume of cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height 

**Calculation:**

Let the sides of the cuboid be L, B & H

So, a = L × B; b = B × H; c = H × L 

abc = (L × B) × (B × H) × (H × L)

⇒ abc = L² × B² × H²

⇒ L × B × H = √abc 

**∴ The volume of cuboid = √abc **

questions.question: A sum of money amounts to Rs.1600 in two years and Rs. 1700 in three years, at compounded interest, compounded annually. What is the rate of interest?

Amount in 3 years = Rs.1700

**Formula used:**

Amount = Principal × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

Let the principal be = P 

1600 = P(1 + R/100)² (1)

1700 = P(1 + R/100)³ (2) 

By (2) ÷ (1) 

⇒ 1700 ÷ 1600 = P(1 + R/100)3 ÷ P(1 + R/100)² 

⇒ 17/16 = (100 + R)³ ÷ (100 + R)²

⇒ 17/16 = (100 + R)/100 

⇒ 1700 = 1600 + 16R 

⇒ R = 100/16 = 6.25 

**∴ The rate of interest is 6.25% [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

The sum of consecutive odd numbers is a perfect square.

∵ 44 + 5 = 49; 49 is the square of 7

questions.question: Avinash, Bhuvnesh and Chaman can complete a piece of work in 20, 30 and 60 days respectively. In how many days can Avinash complete the work if he is assisted by Bhuvnesh and Chaman on every third day?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

No of days Avinash takes = 20 

No of days Bhuvnesh takes = 30

No of days Chaman takes = 60 

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be the LCM of 20, 30 and 60 as being the common multiple. 

LCM (20, 30, 60) = 60 

**Formula used:**

Total work = No of days × Efficiency 

**Calculation:**

Days Total work Efficiency 

Avinash (20) 3

Bhuvnesh (30) 60 units 2 

Chaman (60) 1

On first day Avinash will work alone and on third day Avinash will work with Bhuvnesh and Chaman. 

Day 1 = Avinash = 3 units 

Day 2 = Avinash = 3 units 

Day 3 = Avinash + Bhuvnesh + Chaman = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 units 

Hence, Work done in 3 days = 3 + 3 + 6 = 12 units 

⇒ 3 days × 5 = 12 units × 5

⇒ 15 days = 60 units 

**∴ The required no of days required = 15 days**

questions.question: In a game Rajesh lost (1)/(3) of his money in the first round of the game, in the second round he losses (3)/(5) of his remaining money and in the third round he lost (4)/(7) of the rest. He is left with what part of original sum of monely?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Lost of money in the round 1 = 1/3 

Lost of money in the round 2 = 3/5 of remaining money 

Lost of money in the round 3 = 4/7 of the rest money

**Calculation:**

Let the total money Rajesh has, be the LCM of 3, 5 and 7 just for the convenience of the calculation. 

LCM (3, 5, 7) = 105

Hence, let the total money Rajesh has = 105 

Money he lost in round 1 = 105 × 1/3 = 35

⇒ Remaining money after round 1 = 105 - 35 = 70

Money he lost in round 2 = 70 × 3/5 = 42

⇒ Remaining money after round 2 = 70 - 42 = 28

Money he lost in round 3 = 28 × 4/7 = 16

Now, rest of the money Rajesh has = 28 - 16 = 12

**∴ The fraction of money he is left with to the original money = 12/105 = 4/35**

questions.question: A shopkeeper sold two toys for Rs. 990 each. On the first toy he gained 10% and on the second he lost 10%. Find the total percentage gain or loss.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price of two toys = Rs.990 each 

Increase/ Decrease % = 10% 

**Formula used:**

Loss % = (CP - SP) × 100/CP

SP(selling price) = Cost Price(CP)× (100 + Profit%)/100

SP = CP(100 - loss%)/100

**Calculation: **

Total SP of both toy is = 990 + 990 

⇒ Rs. 1980

CP of the first toy he gained 10%

⇒ 990 × 100/(100 + 10)

⇒ Rs. 900

CP of the second toy he loss 10%

⇒ 990 × (100)/(100 - 10)

⇒ Rs. 1100

Total CP = 900 + 1100

⇒ Rs. 2000

Loss = CP > SP

Loss% = (2000 - 1980)× 100/2000

⇒ 1%

∴ Loss percent = 1%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

**Concept used:**

+ for increase

- for decrease 

Change percent = x + y ± xy/100 

**Calculation:**

Loss/gain percent = + 10% - 10% - 10 × 10/100

⇒ -1%

**∴ Loss percent = 1% **

s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2 

Sides of the triangle = a, b, c

1/2 × 8 × Height = √ 9(9 - 8)(9 - 5)(9 - 5)

⇒ 4 × Height = 3 × 4

⇒ Height = 3 cm 

**∴ The height of the vertex oppsote to the base = 3 cm **

questions.question: By selling an article for Rs.138, a shopkeeper losses 8%. At what price should the article be sold to get a gain of 4%?

Loss percent = 8%

**Formula used:**

Loss percent = (CP - SP) ÷ CP × 100

Selling Price = Cost Price × (100 + profit)%

**Calculation:**

Loss % = (CP - 138) ÷ CP × 100 

⇒ 8 = (CP - 138) ÷ CP × 100 

⇒ 2× CP = 25 × CP - 138 × 25

⇒ 23CP = 138 × 25

⇒ CP = 138 × 25 ÷ 23 = 150

At profit = 4%

⇒ Selling Price = 150 × 104/100 = 156 

**∴ The required selling price = Rs.156**
